clue.text: Trojan boy's heavenly body

blocks.note: first meaning: the beautiful Trojan youth carried off by Zeus to be cupbearer to the gods
second meaning: the largest moon of Jupiter, named after that youth

explanation.surface: A boy from Troy is admired for his gorgeous physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' reads as praise of the boy's looks, but it is a moon in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The myth's cupbearer and Jupiter's biggest satellite share the same name, so one word fits both halves.

clue.text: Get sound to a restricted area

indicators.note: sound tells us to take the words as they are spoken rather than as they are spelt

blocks.note: the first word said out loud, spelt as the start of a different word
taken as written, finishing the spoken pair

explanation.surface: An instruction to make some noise on the way to an off-limits zone.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'get to' is how the answer is pronounced; 'sound' sits between the two words it governs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a quarter of a city to which a minority group was confined, hence a restricted area.

clue.text: Stage direction when these are off

definitions.text: Stage direction when these are off

blocks.clueFragment: Stage direction when these are off
blocks.note: surface reading: some things being cancelled or switched off, mentioned in a script
setter's reading: the famous script direction for sounds made out of the audience's sight, which completes the phrase with 'off'

explanation.surface: A playscript instruction issued when certain things have been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' seems to mean cancelled, but in theatre it means offstage; the direction is the familiar one that also titles Michael Frayn's farce.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounds heard from the wings are marked in scripts with a direction naming these sounds plus the word for offstage.

clue.text: Armies deployed by two Liberals (English) to French port

indicators.note: troops that are deployed are spread out into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, twice
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Troops are sent, alongside a couple of politicians, to a harbour in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseille is France's chief Mediterranean seaport, so it is a port on the French coast.

clue.text: Pirate coined new term for reduction in value

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A buccaneer invented a fresh word for something losing worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coined' looks like part of the story about inventing a word, but its letters belong to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Depreciation is the accounting word for an asset's fall in worth over time.

clue.text: Fate of the musical

blocks.note: first meaning: destiny, a Turkish-Arabic loanword
second meaning: the 1953 Broadway show set in Baghdad

explanation.surface: What became of a stage musical in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means destiny, and it is also the title of the Broadway musical with 'Stranger in Paradise'.

clue.text: Identification for the Isle of Man, in a manner of speaking

blocks.note: ID is the usual short form of identification
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Papers for the Isle of Man, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' reads as a set phrase; only the last three words are the definition. The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression peculiar to a language, a particular way of saying things.

clue.text: Primate and fellow medic unwell

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
a direct synonym

explanation.surface: An ape and a doctor colleague are both feeling poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large West African monkey, and monkeys belong to the primate order.

clue.text: Let's rise anew with boundless energy!

indicators.note: doing something anew means doing it over in a different way, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rousing call to get up again, full of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tireless never flags, which is having energy without any limit.

clue.text: New pie chart and inscription

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters that follow are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a chart is a graph

explanation.surface: A fresh pie chart is presented along with some carved lettering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie chart' looks like a single item, but it splits: the first word is shuffled and the second becomes a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is an engraved inscription on a building or statue, or a motto at the head of a book.

clue.text: A shade backward, goes around pub to get a meal

indicators.note: going backward means the colour word is read from right to left
going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a shade or colour
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A shy figure walks around the local in search of something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A shade backward' sounds like a retiring person, but it is a colour written in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day, eaten in the evening or at midday.

clue.text: Competition for first-class craft

blocks.note: champion as an informal adjective meaning excellent
a craft is a vessel

explanation.surface: A contest for top-quality boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' as an adjective meaning splendid is chiefly northern English usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A championship is a contest held to find the overall winner of a sport.

clue.text: Burden those people on one point

blocks.note: the pronoun for those people
E for east, one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Loading a weight onto some folk at a single spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' looks like a verb for loading people, but here it is the noun for the main idea of a speech or song.
explanation.definitionFit: The burden of a song or argument is its chief recurring idea, which is its theme.

clue.text: Passing a new variety of maple here

indicators.note: a new variety is a different form of something, so the letters take a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Walking past a novel kind of maple tree growing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral things are short-lived, and passing means transient in the same way.

clue.text: Gremlins able to produce statuary from Athens

indicators.note: producing something means making it out of raw material, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mischievous imps manage to create sculpture from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: These sculptures were removed from the Parthenon in Athens by Lord Elgin and are now in the British Museum.

clue.text: Pays attention, absorbed in real practice

indicators.note: something absorbed in another is taken inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, the outer piece
someone paying attention hears

explanation.surface: A student listens carefully, wrapped up in genuine training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pays attention' looks like the subject of a sentence, but it is the piece placed inside the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a performance before it is given for real.

clue.text: Bishop's lost weight, the old rogue

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
having lost weight, one is lighter

explanation.surface: A churchman has slimmed down, the old scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop's' here means bishop is, followed by a description of his state; blighter is British slang for a rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter is a mildly abusive British term for a scamp or rascal, so it fits an old rogue.

clue.text: Brothers and sisters acting together?

blocks.note: surface reading: siblings in a family
setter's reading: trade union members address each other as brother and sister, and their principle is collective action

explanation.surface: Siblings cooperating for once.
explanation.walkthrough: The family picture misleads: in the labour movement, fellow members are called brothers and sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the belief in organised labour bargaining collectively, the principle that workers should act as one.

clue.text: No gents prepared to step into the light during a winter solstice

definitions.note: describes when the answer occurs rather than naming it

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked into shape, so the letters are reordered
stepping into something puts one piece inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, the outer piece

explanation.surface: With no men ready, they come out into the daylight at midwinter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the solstice is when the year's darkest stretch falls, rather than a synonym for it.
explanation.definitionFit: At the winter solstice the sun is lowest, giving the year's shortest day and therefore its maximum hours of darkness.

clue.text: Run son's hard copy

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a hard copy is a printout

explanation.surface: Printing off a boy's document.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprint is to run at full speed over a short distance.

clue.text: The French near building are less encumbered

indicators.note: building something means assembling it from parts, so these letters are put together afresh

blocks.note: LE is French for the
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: French residents close to a construction site have less to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaner means slimmer, carrying less weight or excess, so less burdened.

clue.text: A spirited settlement?

blocks.note: surface reading: a lively, energetic community
setter's reading: a settlement inhabited only by spirits, being deserted by the living

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' normally means lively, the very opposite of an abandoned place; read literally it means full of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserted former settlement is jokingly said to be peopled only by phantoms of past residents.

clue.text: Leaders, take some advice! Reduce staff, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A tip for managers: cut the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' also hints at leading letters, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsars were the emperors of Russia, and the word is now used for anyone in charge of a policy area.

clue.text: One politician the French find is enough

blocks.note: a means one
MP is Member of Parliament
LE is French for the

explanation.surface: French voters decide that a single MP will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, more than sufficient for the purpose.

clue.text: Back at one, father, bearing a venomous creature

indicators.note: back means the short word that follows is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one
pa is an informal word for father
N for north, a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Dad and child are back home, carrying a dangerous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The taipan is an Australian snake, one of the most venomous in the world.

clue.text: He paints foreign actor

indicators.note: something foreign is strange or unfamiliar, so the letters appear in an altered order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An overseas performer who also does painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, from Thespis, the first actor of ancient Greek drama.

clue.text: Don't hit the target twice, that's careless!

blocks.note: the prefix re- means again, so an action done a second time
to fail to hit is to miss

explanation.surface: An archer scolded for going wide two times running.
explanation.walkthrough: Missing twice is missing again, written with the prefix for repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent in one's duty, so careless.

clue.text: Pale trio, ill-informed, producing a hair-remover

indicators.note: being ill-informed means having things wrong, so the letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Three ignorant pasty people come up with a depilatory gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilator is an electric device that pulls hairs out by the root.
